cases.what: Net monthly income for USDA's own published example household
cases.source: fna.usda.gov SNAP eligibility page: 4 people, $1,500 earned, $550 social security, $362 dependent care, $700 shelter. USDA works this through to $1,047.50.

cases.what: Monthly benefit for that same household
cases.source: $994 maximum allotment for four (FY2026 COLA memo) less 30% of $1,047.50 rounded up to $315, per 7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(A)(1). $994 - $315 = $679.

cases.what: A one-person household whose computed benefit falls below the minimum
cases.source: FY2026 Minimum Allotments memo: $24 for one- and two-person households. The regulation derives the same figure as 8% of the $298 one-person maximum.

cases.what: The published gross income limit for a four-person household
cases.source: FY2026 Income Eligibility Standards: $3,483 a month, 130% of poverty.

cases.what: Credit at the earned income amount, one child, tax year 2025
cases.source: Rev. Proc. 2024-40 §3.06: earned income amount $12,730, maximum credit $4,328.

cases.what: Credit at the earned income amount, three or more children, tax year 2026
cases.source: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §3.06: earned income amount $18,290, maximum credit $8,231.

cases.what: Credit at the earned income amount, one child, tax year 2026
cases.source: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §3.06: earned income amount $13,020, maximum credit $4,427. 34% of $13,020 is $4,426.80, and the published maximum rounds it up.

cases.what: Credit reaches zero at the published completed phase-out, two children, single
cases.source: Rev. Proc. 2024-40 §3.06: completed phaseout $57,310 for other filing statuses.

cases.what: One dollar of investment income above the limit forfeits the whole credit
cases.source: Rev. Proc. 2024-40 §3.06(2): limit $11,950 for tax year 2025. IRC 32(i).

cases.what: Two children well below the phase-out threshold
cases.source: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §2.03, recording the OBBBA amendment to IRC 24(h)(2): $2,200 per child. Two children is $4,400, and $50,000 is far below the $200,000 threshold.

cases.what: One child at $210,000, single
cases.source: IRC 24(b): the credit falls $50 for each $1,000 above $200,000. Ten thousand over is ten steps, so $2,200 - $500 = $1,700.

cases.what: A single person inside the QMB limits
cases.source: medicare.gov 2026: QMB income limit $1,350 a month, resource limit $9,950. The Part B premium it covers is $202.90 a month, so $2,434.80 a year.

cases.what: Income above SLMB but inside QI still qualifies
cases.source: medicare.gov 2026: SLMB limit $1,616, QI limit $1,816 for an individual.

cases.what: Income above the widest tier does not qualify
cases.source: medicare.gov 2026: the QI limit of $1,816 is the highest of the three.

cases.what: A single person exactly at the income and resource limits
cases.source: medicare.gov 2026: income limit $23,940, resource limit $18,090.

cases.what: A veteran with no dependents and $10,000 of income
cases.source: va.gov rates from 1 December 2025: MAPR $17,441 with no dependents and no housebound or aid and attendance. The pension is the difference, $7,441.

cases.what: A veteran with one dependent who qualifies for aid and attendance
cases.source: va.gov: MAPR $34,488. With $10,000 of income the pension is $24,488.

cases.what: Assets above the net worth limit disqualify
cases.source: va.gov: the net worth limit from 1 December 2025 is $163,699.

cases.what: One child, $3,000 of care, income at the top of the 35% band
cases.source: IRC 21: expenses capped at $3,000 for one qualifying person, 35% at an income of $15,000 or below. $3,000 x 35% = $1,050.

cases.what: The rate never falls below 20%
cases.source: IRC 21(a)(2): the 35% rate falls a point per $2,000 of income but stops at 20%.

cases.what: Children aged 14 and 15 with $425 a month of daycare: no credit
cases.source: IRC 21(b)(1)(A): a qualifying person is a dependent under 13. Neither child is, so no expense counts and the credit is $0, whatever was paid. Found by the first live end-to-end run, where the answer key and the app both counted every child.

cases.what: A one-person household exactly at 135% of the poverty guideline
cases.source: usac.org 2026 table: $21,546 for one person.

cases.what: One dollar above the table does not qualify on income
cases.source: usac.org 2026 table: $21,546 for one person.

cases.what: The benefit on Tribal lands
cases.source: usac.org: up to $9.25 a month, up to $34.25 on Tribal lands. $34.25 x 12 = $411.

cases.what: A one-person household exactly at 185% of the 2026 poverty guideline
cases.source: 7 CFR 246.7(d) sets WIC at 185% of the federal income guidelines. The 2026 guideline for one person is $15,960, and 185% of that is $29,526.

cases.what: A one-person household one dollar above 130% of the guideline
cases.source: CSFP Income Guidelines 2026: 130% of $15,960 is $20,748.

cases.what: A one-person household exactly at 200% of the guideline
cases.source: 10 CFR 440.3 defines low income as at or below 200% of poverty. 200% of $15,960 is $31,920.

cases.what: Receiving SNAP meets the WIC income test whatever the income figure
cases.source: fna.usda.gov WIC eligibility: a household receiving Medicaid, SNAP or TANF is already income eligible for WIC.

billedNote: OpenRouter key usage before and after the run (1.8252 to 11.3809 USD), read 2026-09-21.
